encounters.cc: Routine pediatric follow-up for intermittent asthma symptoms. Mother reports evening coughing and wheezing episodes occurring one to two times per week for the past month.

lines: Routine pediatric follow-up for intermittent asthma symptoms.
Mother reports evening coughing and wheezing episodes occurring one to two times per week for the past month.
The mother reports that her son has had occasional coughing and wheezing episodes, which seem to occur mostly during the evening or after playing outside.
These episodes have been occurring about once or twice a week for the past month.
He is up to date with his vaccinations.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg per actuation, 1-2 puffs by mouth every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing or shortness of breath
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Elementary school student.
On physical examination, the boy is in no acute distress, and his vital signs are within normal limits.
Lung auscultation reveals no wheezing or other abnormal sounds at rest.
The rest of the examination is unremarkable.
A spirometry test is performed, showing a forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) of 95% predicted and an FEV1/forced vital capacity (FVC) ratio within the normal range.

encounters.cc: Three-week history of spreading, slightly raised rash on trunk and upper arms that began as a single oval patch after a mild sore throat.

lines: Three-week history of spreading, slightly raised rash on trunk and upper arms that began as a single oval patch after a mild sore throat.

The patient is an 8-year-old male with mild intermittent asthma, last evaluated in January 2020 for routine follow-up of respiratory symptoms, who presents with a three-week history of a spreading, slightly raised rash on his trunk and upper arms.
The eruption began as a single oval patch and later developed into multiple similar lesions.
His mother notes that the rash started after he had a mild sore throat, which resolved without treatment.
The lesions are described as slightly scaly, oval-shaped, and arranged in a parallel pattern along skin folds, but they are not painful or pruritic.
The child is otherwise well, afebrile, and has no mucosal involvement.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg per actuation, 1-2 puffs by mouth every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing or shortness of breath
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Elementary school student.
On examination, the initial lesion is larger than the others, and all have a fine peripheral scale with central clearing.
KOH prep from a scraped lesion is negative for hyphae.
The physician reassures the mother that this condition is self-limited and requires no specific treatment.

lines: Four-day history of fever up to 39.2°C, productive cough, and decreased activity requiring urgent evaluation.

encounters.cc: Fell off bicycle without helmet, landed on side, with immediate crying but no loss of consciousness or amnesia.

lines: Fell off bicycle without helmet, landed on side, with immediate crying but no loss of consciousness or amnesia.
The patient, with mild intermittent asthma and prior pneumonia in this department six months ago, presents following the fall.
He landed on his side and did not lose consciousness.
His parents report that he cried immediately after the fall but calmed down within a few minutes.
He has been alert and oriented, with no amnesia for the event.
His medical history is significant only for mild intermittent asthma,.
He takes for which he uses an albuterol inhaler as needed.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg per actuation, 1-2 puffs by mouth every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing or shortness of breath
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Elementary school student.
On examination, the child is playful and interactive, with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 15.
He complains of a mild headache but has no vomiting, no seizure activity, and no focal neurological deficits.
There is a small abrasion on his right elbow and a contusion on his right temporal area without overlying scalp hematoma.
and the rest of the physical examination is unremarkable.

encounters.cc: Rash and joint pain for two days following an upper respiratory tract infection last week. Rash began on buttocks and spread to lower legs, non-blanching and slightly raised.

lines: Rash and joint pain for two days following an upper respiratory tract infection last week.
Rash began on buttocks and spread to lower legs, non-blanching and slightly raised.
The patient is a 10-year-old male with a history of mild intermittent asthma and pityriasis rosea who presents with a rash that began on his buttocks and has spread to his lower legs.
The lesions do not blanch with pressure and are slightly raised.
He also complains of pain in his knees and ankles.
His mother reports that he had an upper respiratory tract infection one week ago, which has since resolved.
The boy has a past medical history of mild intermittent asthma.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg per actuation, 1-2 puffs by mouth every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing or shortness of breath

On examination, the child appears uncomfortable but is not in acute distress.
Examination of the lower extremities reveals palpable purpura concentrated on the buttocks and extending down to the lower legs.
The joints are tender to palpation but there is no significant swelling or redness.

lines: Submerged in swimming pool for approximately two minutes, initially unresponsive but regained consciousness after rescue breaths administered by lifeguard.
